newsitem.title: UK: British factory prices fall in June.
newsitem.headline: British factory prices fall in June.

text.p: Prices of British manufactured goods fell by 0.2 percent in June, their largest drop since July 1996, the Office for National Statistics said Monday.
Analysts said the figures showed inflationary pressures in Britain's sluggish manufacturing sector remained weak and boded well for the country's crucial retail price inflation rate.
The decline in June output prices reverses May's 0.2 percent rise but still took the yearly growth rate up to 1.1 percent from 1.0 percent in May.

The strength of the pound sterling provided some good news for hard-pressed manufacturers, further trimming prices of fuel and raw materials and leaving scope for relatively healthy profit margins. Input prices fell 0.8 percent on a seasonally adjusted basis, after a moderate increase of 0.6 percent in May.

On a year-on-year basis, input prices registered their 13th successive monthly drop, at 8.6 percent, forced lower by weaker prices for oil and other commodities, reflecting sterling's meteoric gain of some 25 percent since last August.
The high level of sterling has made British exports more expensive in foreign currency terms, leading some manufacturers to cut prices in order to remain competitive.
The government said that printing and publishing prices had fallen by 1.7 percent between May and June as companies struggled to maintain their competitive edge.
Analysts warned that there was little chance of an early halt to the pound's progress while expectations remain of further rises in official interest rates.
The Bank of England, with its eyes on the inflation horizon two years ahead, raised interest rates to 6.75 percent, from 6.5 last week, the third rise in as many months.
Some economists say rates could rise again as early as next month.
